source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: NOAA GHCN-Daily version 3.35-upd-2026102617 (ghcnd-version.txt; readme Version 3.35): by_year/2024.csv (root; header ID, YEAR/MONTH/DAY, ELEMENT, DATA VALUE, M-FLAG, Q-FLAG, S-FLAG, OBS-TIME added per readme-by_year.txt; tens of millions of station-day-element lines, so the builder samples 1,000,000 records; the file is 'updated daily for the entire period of record', so the download date fixes the version) left-joined to ghcnd-stations.txt on ID, then to ghcnd-states.txt on STATE = CODE and to ghcnd-inventory.txt on (ID, ELEMENT), the three fixed-width files converted to ghcn/ghcnd-stations.csv, ghcn/ghcnd-states.csv and ghcn/ghcnd-inventory.csv with the readme's field names of sections IV, VI and VII; the FIPS country (ghcnd-countries.txt) is not joined since it would need the ID prefix; dropped the inventory's LATITUDE and LONGITUDE (they repeat the station's coordinates), nothing else.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: ghcnd_readme-by_station.txt: "Each element-day is provided on a separate line and all files are updated daily for the entire period of record."; ghcnd_readme-by_year.txt: "The following information serves as a definition of each field in one line of data covering one station-day."; ghcnd_readme.txt, section III: "When data are available for the same time from more than one source, the highest priority source is chosen according to the following priority order (from highest to lowest)"
truth.justification: A line of the yearly file is one station-day of one element, each element-day on its own line, and when several sources report the same time one source is chosen, so a station, date and element carry one value with its three flags and observation time.

audit.quote: Each element-day is provided on a separate line and all files are updated daily for the entire period of record. || The following information serves as a definition of each field in one line of data covering one station-day. || Each record in a file contains one month of daily data. || When data are available for the same time from more than one source, the highest priority source is chosen according to the following priority order (from highest to lowest): || The OBS-TIME field is populated with the observation times contained in NOAA/NCEI's HOMR station history database.
audit.source: ghcnd_readme-by_station.txt, whole file || ghcnd_readme-by_year.txt, whole file || ghcnd_readme.txt, section III || ghcnd_readme.txt, section III, SFLAG1 || ghcnd_readme-by_year.txt, whole file

truth.clause: ghcnd_readme.txt, section IV: "ID         is the station identification code."; ghcnd_readme.txt, section II: "ghcnd-stations.txt:   List of stations and their metadata (e.g., coordinates)"; ghcnd_readme.txt, section III: "Each ".dly" file contains data for one station.  The name of the file corresponds to a station's identification code."
truth.justification: ID identifies one station and ghcnd-stations.txt lists each station with its metadata, so the ID determines the station's coordinates, elevation, state, name, flags and WMO number.

audit.quote: ID is the station identification code. || ghcnd-stations.txt: List of stations and their metadata (e.g., coordinates) || Each ".dly" file contains data for one station. The name of the file corresponds to a station's identification code.
audit.source: ghcnd_readme.txt, section IV || ghcnd_readme.txt, section II || ghcnd_readme.txt, section III

truth.clause: ghcnd_readme.txt, section VI: "CODE       is the POSTAL code of the U.S. state/territory or Canadian province where the station is located" and "NAME       is the name of the state, territory or province."; ghcnd_readme.txt, section II: "ghcnd-states.txt:     List of U.S. state and Canadian Province codes used in ghcnd-stations.txt"
truth.justification: The postal code identifies one state, territory or province and the file lists each code with its name; section IV calls STATE 'the U.S. postal code for the state (for U.S. stations only)' while section VI includes Canadian provinces, so stations elsewhere have a blank STATE and a missing STATE NAME, which does not break the dependency.

audit.quote: CODE is the POSTAL code of the U.S. state/territory or Canadian province where the station is located || NAME is the name of the state, territory or province. || ghcnd-states.txt: List of U.S. state and Canadian Province codes used in ghcnd-stations.txt || STATE is the U.S. postal code for the state (for U.S. stations only).
audit.source: ghcnd_readme.txt, section VI || ghcnd_readme.txt, section VI || ghcnd_readme.txt, section II || ghcnd_readme.txt, section IV

truth.clause: ghcnd_readme.txt, section II: "ghcnd-inventory.txt:  File listing the periods of record for each station and element"; ghcnd_readme.txt, section VII: "FIRSTYEAR  is the first year of unflagged data for the given element." and "LASTYEAR   is the last year of unflagged data for the given element."
truth.justification: The inventory holds one period of record per station and element, so the pair determines its first and last year.

audit.quote: ghcnd-inventory.txt: File listing the periods of record for each station and element || FIRSTYEAR is the first year of unflagged data for the given element. || LASTYEAR is the last year of unflagged data for the given element.
audit.source: ghcnd_readme.txt, section II || ghcnd_readme.txt, section VII || ghcnd_readme.txt, section VII

truth.clause: ghcnd_readme.txt, section IV: "GSN FLAG   is a flag that indicates whether the station is part of the GCOS Surface Network (GSN). The flag is assigned by cross-referencing the number in the WMOID field with the official list of GSN stations." and "Blank = non-GSN station or WMO Station number not available"
truth.justification: The flag is assigned as a function of the WMO number (whether it is on the official GSN list), and a blank WMO number gives a blank flag, so stations with the same WMO ID carry the same flag.

audit.quote: GSN FLAG is a flag that indicates whether the station is part of the GCOS Surface Network (GSN). The flag is assigned by cross-referencing the number in the WMOID field with the official list of GSN stations. || Blank = non-GSN station or WMO Station number not available
audit.source: ghcnd_readme.txt, section IV || ghcnd_readme.txt, section IV, GSN FLAG values

gold_design_note: No normalized design is published; the 3NF designs of Sigma* are synthesized.

mined.algorithm: fdmine.py: exact discovery of all minimal FDs in the style of HyFD (no HyFD binary was available); the complete set of minimal FDs is unique, so it equals HyFD's output
